summary.text: Dark matter is an invisible form of matter that does not interact with light, and it is implied by gravitational effects that visible matter cannot explain.
In the standard Lambda-CDM model, the universe's mass-energy is 5% ordinary matter, 26.8% dark matter and 68.2% dark energy.
It is not known to interact with ordinary matter except through gravity, so the leading idea is an undiscovered particle such as a WIMP or an axion.

facts.label: Share of mass-energy
facts.value: 26.8% of the universe in the standard model

facts.label: Zwicky's estimate
facts.value: The Coma Cluster had about 400 times more mass than visible

facts.label: In our Solar System
facts.value: All of it out to Neptune weighs about a large asteroid

facts.value: Cold, warm or hot, sorted by velocity

items.prompt: Galaxies near the edge of a cluster move fast, yet the gravity of the galaxies we can see is far too small to hold them in. What did Fritz Zwicky infer?

options.label: The galaxies we see must be much heavier than they look
Unseen matter supplies the extra pull that holds the cluster together
The cluster was flying apart and would soon vanish
Gravity must be much weaker at the edge of a cluster

items.explain: The visible galaxies' gravity was far too small for such fast orbits, so he inferred unseen matter provided the mass and pull that holds the cluster together.

items.prompt: Researchers try to catch dark matter in a laboratory, but it is very hard to spot. What makes it so hard to detect?

options.label: It is not known to interact with matter or radiation except through gravity
It exists only in galaxy halos far away
It disappears when it is in a laboratory
It is made entirely of ordinary atoms that are too small

items.explain: Apart from gravity, it is not known to interact with ordinary matter and radiation, which makes it difficult to detect in the laboratory.

items.prompt: A friend says dark matter must be thick around us, tugging on the planets. What does the Solar System actually show?

options.label: Dark matter far outweighs normal matter here
It weighs about as much as normal matter does here
Its local density is much less than normal matter
There is none of it anywhere nearby

items.explain: Dark matter is dense in a galaxy's halo, but its local density in the Solar System is much less than that of normal matter.

items.prompt: Some scientists suggest that gravity itself is different from what we think, instead of there being dark matter. What do the theories so far suggest?

options.label: They already explain every observation at once
They prove that dark matter cannot exist
They all rely on dark energy
Some form of dark matter still seems needed even with modified gravity

items.explain: None of the proposed modified gravity theories can describe all the evidence at once, suggesting some form of dark matter would still be required.

items.prompt: Astronomers call some dark matter cold, some warm and some hot. What decides which label it gets?

options.label: How bright it looks to our telescopes
How fast it moves, its velocity
How close it happens to sit to a star
The type of galaxy that it sits inside

items.explain: Dark matter is classified as cold, warm or hot according to velocity, or more precisely its free streaming length.

items.prompt: In the 1970s, astronomers argued that galaxies sit inside halos of unseen matter. What observation helped back this up?

options.label: The shape of galaxy rotation curves
The colour of the faintest stars
The number of known planets
The age of the Solar System

items.explain: The shape of galaxy rotation curves was one of the observations used as evidence for halos of dark matter around galaxies.
